subject.title: Cron Jobs Calendar View for Control UI

question: Should OpenClaw accept a repaired 24-hour Cron Jobs timeline as the first product slice, require the broader daily/week calendar and drag-and-drop design first, or defer this Control UI feature?
rationale: The request is a new user-facing Control UI surface rather than a broken current contract, and the linked PR implements only part of the requested scope while needing a substantial rebase.

options.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
options.body: Rebase or recreate the linked PR on the current Cron page and accept the 24-hour timeline as an intentional first slice while tracking or rejecting the broader scope separately.

options.title: Design Full Calendar Scope
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define daily, weekly, quick-stat, validation, and drag-and-drop editing behavior together.

options.title: Defer Core Calendar View
options.body: Leave the current list/run-history UI as core for now and close or defer the linked implementation after documenting the product decision.

recommendation.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
recommendation.body: Rebase or recreate the linked PR on the current Cron page and accept the 24-hour timeline as an intentional first slice while tracking or rejecting the broader scope separately.

likelyOwner.reason: BunsDev has the strongest recent Control UI view-surface ownership signal among the likely owners, so they are the best available routing candidate for this product-scope choice.
